turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
I asked you a question, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Owen: Mom, I'm sorry. I used ChatGPT for the whole thing.
Don't put words in my son's mouth, Hale. If you have something in writing, show me. Otherwise, who decided on the zero?
You heard him. He just admitted it.

I heard you, Hale, and I'm writing down "He just admitted it." My son doesn't lie, and I don't take accusations without paper. Show me something with a date on it, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
Owen, can you tell your mom what you told me on November 2?
You're asking me to take your word again, Hale. If you spoke with Owen on November 2, you'll have made a note of it, so show me. And then explain why nobody phoned me before that zero went in.
Meredith, respond to Owen, and then write what Owen says back.
Don't script my conversations with my son, Hale. I'm still waiting on your note from November 2.
I'll talk to my son at home, Hale. In this room, your own procedure says you call the parent before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. That's what we're discussing.
